coverageSpotVerification.detail: coverage-manifest-all.json maps all 69 suite-required assertions across M1–M6 and M8 and revalidates clean against the frozen instrument/metering/coverage-manifest.mjs for every milestone at runScope full and pin social-messenger@0.3.8-m8. Every sampled mapping drives the assertion's real observable rather than a proxy: m8-a01's test recomputes all six lifetime totals from raw SQL over the store and compares them to the insights query; m3-a15 double-seeds each installed segment and deep-equals full table snapshots; m6-a13 shells the frozen fixture validator. No dishonest mapping found. Two weaknesses recorded without changing the verdict: (1) m3-a11's mapped test only ever quotes a message already inside the viewport, so it cannot observe the scroll failure the grader found; (2) m2-a13's "no preview card" is proxied by an iframe count, which would miss a non-iframe unfurl. Note also that the documented coverage-manifest.json is rewritten by every suite run to hold only the last milestone; coverage-manifest-all.json is the complete artifact.

defects.summary: The M8 acceptance suite advances the dev server clock by 25 h (snapback4 clock advance 25h) and never restores it, so every row it then writes is stamped ~25 h in the future. Those future-dated posts permanently occupy the whole first page of the newest-first Global feed, and the clock offset survives for the life of the backend process. Running the documented suites in their documented order m1 -> m8 therefore leaves the lane unable to pass its own M2 suite again.
defects.evidence: grading/trace.md#d-01 — reproduced 3/3 (twice on the delivered store, once after a clean store ran m1..m8 in order); 22 posts dated 2026-10-07 in the delivered store against a 2026-10-06 wall clock; server insights.asOf measured +25.10 h from local time

defects.summary: Tapping a quoted excerpt loads the original message but does not scroll to it when the original lies outside the already-rendered window. The quoted-reply jump is the M3 checklist observable (m3-a11); it works only in the trivial case where the original is already on screen.

O1.anchorsCited: Between the 60 anchor ("M1–M4 solid, later milestones patchy or failed on cap") and the 90 anchor ("every in-scope milestone green, including platform-proof artifacts"), with every milestone of the full run scope in the denominator regardless of status.
O1.justification: 100 of the 119 frozen assertions pass under independent execution, 1 fails (m3-a11), 18 are not-run. Per milestone: M1 13/13, M2 27/27, M3 14/15, M4 12/12, M5 12/12, M6 6/13, M7 0/9, M8 16/18. The lane is clearly past the 60 anchor — M1–M5 are solid rather than patchy and M6/M8 are solid on everything they actually proved. It is well short of 90 for two structural reasons: a whole in-scope milestone (M7) was never attempted and scores its checklist not-passed, and no platform-proof artifact exists anywhere — the 7 M6 and 2 M8 simulator assertions have no harness recording at all (choreography summaries record ios-simulator-m6 / ios-simulator-m8 as "not-recorded"), and the only native artifacts shipped are Hermes bundle exports. Quality where built is high: everything I re-executed independently matched, including all server-side authorization refusals.

O2.anchorsCited: Between the 60 anchor ("a few medium defects off the happy path") and the 90 anchor ("only cosmetic nits"), nearer 60.
O2.justification: Beyond-checklist defects: one major (d-01, the M8 suite's unrestored 25 h clock advance, which deterministically breaks the lane's own M2 suite in the documented order and leaves the delivered store with future-dated rows dominating the Global feed), four minor (d-03 undocumented backend.pid dependency that kills the M8 digest leg from the documented startup; d-04 stale .replay resume state aborting with an opaque E_AUTH; d-05 a non-waiting suite assertion that flakes; d-06 a self-overwriting coverage manifest) and one cosmetic (d-07 N_SPARSE_FILTER on the Following read). What keeps this above 60 is that none of these are product-correctness or trust defects: across extensive independent API probing I found no wrong data, no crash, no authorization gap — counts, idempotent set/clear intents, receipt watermarks, expiry and asset revocation all behaved exactly as specified. What keeps it well below 90 is that d-01 is reproducible, self-inflicted and leaves the delivered lane in a state where its own documented acceptance entrypoint fails. d-02 is listed for evidence but is the m3-a11 checklist failure itself and is scored in O1, not double-counted here.

O4.anchorsCited: Above the 30 anchor ("cold-start offline shows an empty or broken app"); the 90 anchor ("reads, ordered queued writes, receipt transitions, and offline search all behave as specced on the native proof — on full runs including M8's durable-queue restart and multi-device convergence evidence") is unreachable because no native proof exists; the 60 anchor's failure modes ("offline writes lost or mis-ordered, or receipts wrong after flush") are not present.
O4.justification: Scored only from the harness's structured receipts, never from builder assertions. What the harness actually recorded is clean: M5 warm-offline-search-over-synced-messages passed (3.97 s); M6 offline-message-queue-flush-in-order passed with flushMs 959.5; M8 m8-a15-dual-offline-convergence passed (firstFlushMs 1071.8, secondFlushMs 2169.4, no loss, no duplicates) and m8-a16-dual-offline-receipts passed (firstReadMs 29.2, secondReadMs 30.3). Nothing offline was observed lost, mis-ordered or wrong after flush. What is entirely missing is the native half the dimension is built around: all seven M6 cold-start-offline simulator assertions and both M8 durable-restart simulator assertions have no artifact — the segment summaries carry ios-simulator-m6 and ios-simulator-m8 as pass:null, status "not-recorded", requiredForGreen:false, and the lane ships only .hbc bundle exports. O4 explicitly weighs "honesty of any gap between claim and guarantee", and the gap here is declared rather than overclaimed: the receipts mark the legs not-recorded with a reason and README.md states simulator smoke was outside this run's proof scope, with no offline claim resting on it. Half the dimension demonstrated cleanly, half never demonstrated but honestly declared.

O5.bandRationale: First-match over the frozen order 0, 30, 60, 90, 75. Band 0 does not fire: I independently re-verified the invariant manifest and it conforms exactly — the receipt's actionLog sha256 equals the frozen scale.log digest, all 167,157 actions settled with 0 failures, both checkpoints match their frozen prefix counts and prefix SHAs (10%: 24,777 / f1f4abf9…, 50%: 88,057 / f3ce5872…), every perEntityCount at 10%, 50% and 100% matches expectedState with zero mismatches, and namedFixtures verified true at every checkpoint; the replay cap was not exhausted (capFractionUsed 0.3818 of 14,400 s, capExhausted false). Band 30 does not fire on any evidence available to me: no scored probe timed out, errored or OOMed, because this wave committed no probe set (wave.probeSetSha256 = none-uncommitted), and the lane's own non-scored continuity probes returned at all three checkpoints with p95 between 3.3 ms and 42.9 ms. Band 60 does not fire: replay used 38.2% of its cap, well under 80%. Band 90 cannot fire: it requires every probe's observed ceiling utilization to be <=50%, and with no committed probe set there are no scored probes and no frozen ceilings to measure utilization against, so that condition is not established. First match therefore lands on 75. The band is limited by the wave's missing probe set, not by anything observed in the replay record, which is fully conformant.

notes: N=1 calibration run, not a claim-eligible wave. Three wrapper-mandated deviations from the frozen protocol are recorded here and in the trace. (1) No holdout probe set was committed for this wave, so execution-order phase 4 was skipped, wave.probeSetSha256 is the literal string none-uncommitted and probeResults is empty by instruction; no probes were invented. (2) The Claude family has not passed the grader calibration gate, so grader.calibrationPassed is false and this grade is labelled uncalibrated-grader; sameFamilyGraded is false (the builder lane records harness model gpt-6-astra). (3) Timing-sensitive checks are judged best-of-3 and host load is recorded beside every timing record: this machine carried 1-minute load averages between 76 and 221 (3 users, other lanes active) throughout the session, which is the direct cause of several builder-suite legs aborting on settlement timeouts that pass under independent execution. O3 is recorded as null and this is NOT an applicability judgement: applicability.json makes O3 applicable here (M6 green, M1-M5 attempted), but the frozen rule scores O3 "from the wave's secret rotated holdout probes only" and no such probe set exists for this wave, so no rule-following score can be produced. Scoring O3 from the checklist's own trust observations would violate that rule, and inventing probes was forbidden, so the dimension is applicable-but-unscorable. For the record, and explicitly not as O3 input, every server-side authorization check I made during independent checklist execution was correctly enforced: revoked-token whoAmI denied E_AUTH, self-follow refused SELF_FOLLOW, non-admin member removal and group rename refused ADMIN_REQUIRED, post-window edit refused EDIT_WINDOW_CLOSED, asset after delete-for-everyone denied E_ASSET_UNKNOWN, asset after view-once denied E_ASSET_VIEWED with raw HTTP 410, expired disappearing message absent server-side with its media revoked, and activity in a chat the target is not a member of contributed nothing to that user's digest counts. The 18 M8 assertion results are not in this file because the frozen grader-report schema permits only the 101 M1-M7 IDs; they are written to grading/m8-assertion-results.json in the same record shape, with no ID duplicated across the two files. Grading ran against a reset backend store: .snapback4/, .replay/ and data/ are gitignored, so "from a clean checkout" means they are absent; the delivered store is preserved under grading/delivered-store-backup/. The lane's choreography copy is byte-identical to the frozen instrument copy (only an added package-lock.json and node_modules differ), so its receipts come from the unmodified harness.
